model: Intelligent Follow-up Concrete Placing Pump HG18
name: BMR Intelligent Follow-up Concrete Placing Pump HG18
summary: Floor-mounted concrete placing boom with 18 m reach that places slab concrete along a preset path on its own, follows one worker's joystick, or runs by remote or by hand. BMR says it cuts placing crews and gives more even pours that need less levelling.

germany.statusNote: BMR sells direct from Shenzhen and names no EU distributor; no CE statement on the product page read (the BMR measuring robot page does state CE, this one does not). No German offer found.

specs.label: Minimum weight for transfer between floors
specs.conditions: value in brackets as printed by BMR

specs.label: Installation
specs.value: preformed slab hole 1.2×1.2–1.5×1.5 m or lift shaft 2.1×2.1–2.3×2.3 m

specs.label: Operating modes
specs.value: automatic (preset path), follow-up (one-person joystick), remote, manual
specs.quote: Automatic mode (automatic placing according to preset path)Follow-up mode (single-person joystick operation)Remote mode (remote operation of boom and arm)Manual mode (traditional manual pulling)

specs.label: Placing manpower needed
specs.conditions: follow-up mode vs. manual placing, maker claim; levelling workload 13 % lower in automatic mode
specs.quote: only 30% of the manpower is needed to complete the placing work

notes: Stationary placing boom: set on the slab or in the lift shaft and moved up floor by floor with the crane; it does not drive.
The boom is the single 'arm'; tool = concrete delivery hose at the boom tip.
BMR's figures are marked as coming from the Bright Dream laboratory.
